nodes.label: Blade Cleanup Readiness Verdict: NO-GO
nodes.rationale: Full manual SPA validation was not executed, the local SPA lacks VITE_PUSHER_* so realtime UI is unvalidated, and several admin modules (user roles, metrics, catalogs, profile, alert detail, device/sensor CRUD) still depend on Blade, so Fase 6B cannot start yet.

nodes.label: SEC-002: Global Legacy IoT API Key
nodes.norm_label: sec-002: global legacy iot api key
nodes.rationale: Ingestion still accepts a global legacy API_KEY besides per-device keys; if leaked it could inject readings into any active sensor. Recommendation: rely on per-device keys and retire the global key.

nodes.label: SEC-004: SMTP Password Stored as System Setting
nodes.norm_label: sec-004: smtp password stored as system setting
nodes.rationale: SMTP password is never returned via API but is stored in system_settings; direct DB access would expose it. Recommendation: encrypt sensitive SystemSetting values or move them to environment/secret manager.

nodes.label: Alerts table lacks context snapshot
nodes.rationale: alerts table stores only sensor_reading_id/alert_rule_id/resolved, reconstructing severity/message/value via live relations to sensor_readings/alert_rules/sensors/devices/labs; separating the alerts module would require snapshotting this context to avoid dependency on live rows.

nodes.label: DashboardMetricsServiceTest constructor non-conformity
nodes.rationale: DashboardMetricsService constructor changed to require AlertService but 3 unit tests were not updated to inject it, causing ArgumentCountError; tracked as an open non-conformity blocking full ISO 9001/12207 quality-control closure.

nodes.label: NewSensorReading::handle() likely dead code
nodes.rationale: NewSensorReading::handle() calls checkForAlert() but the event is never registered as a listener anywhere found, suggesting either dead code or an abandoned earlier design intention.

nodes.label: Email side effect embedded in Alert model
nodes.norm_label: email side effect embedded in alert model
nodes.rationale: Alert::sendDangerAlertEmail mutates global config() and calls Mail::send from within the model, coupling persistence model to SMTP infrastructure; recommended to move to a dedicated notifier service/job.

nodes.label: ICONTEC/ISO alignment (not certification) declaration policy
nodes.rationale: Repository declares technical/documentary alignment with ICONTEC and ISO norms deliberately without claiming formal external certification, since no accredited body audit was performed; every compliance claim must link concrete file/line evidence or a verification command.

nodes.label: Alert threshold comparison is inclusive (<=, >=)
nodes.rationale: AlertService threshold check uses belowMin = value <= min_value and aboveMax = value >= max_value, but UI copy describes exclusive comparison ('menor a' / 'supera'), a documented UI/backend mismatch.

nodes.label: mail_enabled toggle not enforced
nodes.rationale: mail_enabled setting exists in config/UI but neither Alert::sendDangerAlertEmail nor NotificationService::notifyDangerAlertByEmail check it, so danger alerts can email even when the toggle is off — identified pain point for module separation.

nodes.label: Real SMTP credentials in SystemSettingsSeeder
nodes.rationale: database/seeders/SystemSettingsSeeder.php historically carried real-looking SMTP credentials in plain text; flagged as security risk requiring rotation before reuse, blocks safe module separation if replicated as-is.

nodes.label: Two dynamic mail-configuration styles
nodes.rationale: EmailConfigController::testEmail uses legacy config keys (driver/host/etc) while Alert::sendDangerAlertEmail uses mail.default/mail.from/mail.mailers.smtp — inconsistent dynamic config mutation approaches that can drift.

nodes.label: Idempotency Ledger via status Column
nodes.rationale: The raw_sensor_events.status column serves as the idempotency ledger for the consumer group. Status transitions (received → processed → failed) within the same transaction ensure exactly-once processing semantics without requiring external deduplication.

nodes.label: MQTT Ingestion
nodes.rationale: The ingestion service receives raw MQTT payloads, validates minimal structure, normalizes to the backend raw contract, and enqueues durably via SQLite WAL before posting to the backend. Separation of concerns: MQTT reception and raw event publication are isolated from downstream processing.

nodes.label: QC Validation Gate
nodes.rationale: When payload.qc.valid is strictly false, the raw receipt is preserved for audit but no normalized readings are created and no alert rules are evaluated. This prevents corrupted data from entering the processing pipeline while maintaining auditability.

nodes.label: Clean Tracked Worktree Requirement
nodes.rationale: The harness requires a clean tracked Git worktree before Docker preflight to prevent Compose bind mounts from executing modified source while labeling the result with the prior HEAD SHA. Untracked files do not affect this identity check.

nodes.label: Audit Lifecycle Fixture Fix
nodes.rationale: The audit lifecycle previously selected fixture sensor 2/202 which was already one of the four default widgets, producing a no-op selection. The runner now selects the final fixture device's first sensor, proving a real add instead of a no-op.

nodes.label: 44px Minimum Touch Target Remediation
nodes.rationale: Actual controls now have 44px minimum targets: dashboard buttons/selects/ranges/edit controls, mobile menu/account, demo toggle, resource actions/status control, and modal close actions. The resource CSS no longer overrides the global button target with 34px/36px values.

nodes.label: useLabWorkspace Authorization Fix
nodes.rationale: useLabWorkspace incorrectly treated a user's personal dashboard layout as an admin capability. Fix: dashboard editing is now available for temporary guest drafts and ordinary authenticated users, with save() still requiring authentication as the authorization boundary.

nodes.label: Live Infrastructure Evidence Gap
nodes.rationale: No real Pusher-compatible WebSocket, API, Redis, Debezium, or CDC consumer stack was available. The in-app Browser integration was unavailable (missing plugin module). Repository Playwright Chromium was used as fallback. Fixture rows remain mocked API evidence — this is a live-evidence GAP, not a test pass.

nodes.label: Architecture Audit and Implementation Plan
nodes.description: Full architecture audit of refraccion branch. Executive verdict: not fully event-driven. Three Vue timers discover state through REST (10s alerts, 5s dashboard alerts, 2s sensor monitors). Raw ingestion stores receipt but no consumer exists. Root causes: RC1 split state ownership, RC2 incomplete domain-event coverage, RC3 non-atomic persist+publish, RC4 missing durable consumer ops, RC5 transport≠projection lifecycle, RC6 no behavioral mobile/a11y test. 9 mobile findings (M01-M09). Complete polling inventory (7 items). Event catalog with 6 event types. Observer/listener matrix. Redis Streams audit. WebSocket/Echo architecture. 10-stage migration roadmap. Implementation backlog (TASK-001..012). Complexity review: CDC is biggest over-engineering risk, DLQ should reuse failed_jobs, full reconnect protocol is more than v1 needs.
nodes.rationale: The foundational audit document that drives the entire migration plan. Contains the root cause analysis, polling inventory, event catalog, architecture decisions, and complexity review that informed PLAN.md.

nodes.label: Project Changelog
nodes.description: Keep a Changelog format. v0.1.0 (2026-09-09): initial v2 release with transactional outbox, Redis Streams, Vue 3 SPA, Laravel 12 backend, Python ingestion, Docker Compose (8 services). Unreleased: durable publication pipeline (outboxes + Debezium + CDC streams + consumers), public minimal API for graph and restricted sensor series, private channels for alerts and device status, BackendClient exponential backoff, MonitorCard/SensorMonitorBoard ownership split, MigrationIntegrityTest.
nodes.rationale: Tracks the project's evolution from v0.1.0 through the current refraccion branch. Documents the transition from legacy relay to Debezium CDC and the addition of private broadcasting channels.

nodes.label: Project Instructions (CLAUDE.md)
nodes.description: Root project instructions for Claude Code. Defines monorepo shape: back/ (Laravel 12), front/ (Vue 3), ingestion_service/ (Python), script_datos.py. Commands for backend, frontend, Docker, and ingestion. Architecture: routes → controllers → services → models → observers → events → broadcast + mail. Two ingestion paths: legacy POST /api/sensors/{sensor}/readings (API key) and raw-first POST /api/ingestion/events (token). Auth: Sanctum tokens, IoT API key, admin middleware. Rate limits: api-read 120/min, api-write 60/min, auth-login 5/min. Known gaps: no browser test suite, incomplete alert resolution/device status propagation, SMTP credentials in seeder.
nodes.rationale: The authoritative project overview for Claude Code agents. Defines the monorepo structure, all build/test commands, the two ingestion paths, auth mechanisms, and known gaps that constrain implementation.

Superseded by current code and repository-state docs. Describes Blade as primary UI, observers as full publication path, and ingestion without CDC — all outdated. Institution: UNAB, Bucaramanga, 2026.
nodes.rationale: Historical academic documentation. Explicitly marked as superseded; useful only for understanding the project's academic alignment and institutional context. Not a source of runtime truth.

nodes.label: Project README (verified state)
nodes.description: Comprehensive project README with verifiable state table. SPA Vue 3 with public and authenticated routes. Public surface: only GET /api/public/graph/bootstrap and GET /api/public/graph/sensors/{sensor}/series (filtered by public_monitoring_enabled). Ingestion: raw-first with raw_sensor_events + raw_event_outboxes in one transaction. Debezium captures binlog, consumers normalize and deliver domain events. Auth: Sanctum, API key, ingestion token, admin middleware. Domain model: LAB→DEVICE→SENSOR→SENSOR_READING, ALERT_RULE, ALERT, RAW_SENSOR_EVENT, RAW_EVENT_OUTBOX, DOMAIN_EVENT_OUTBOX. Alert cycle: reading → AlertService evaluates rules → alert + domain outbox → CDC → domain:consume → broadcasting. Complete API inventory with access boundaries.
nodes.rationale: The most up-to-date verified-state document. Contains the complete API inventory, domain model, access boundaries, Docker Compose instructions, and diagnostic procedures. Supersedes DOCUMENTACION_PROYECTO.md for runtime truth.

nodes.label: RBAC/Security Remediation Summary
nodes.description: 8-phase remediation: Phase 0 auth contract fix (/auth/me canonical response), Phase 1 RBAC foundation (roles/permissions/role_user tables, 4 roles: guest/user/admin/superadmin), Phase 2 RBAC integration (Role/Permission models, EnsureUserHasPermission middleware, AuditService, RoleController, policies updated), Phase 3 retire is_admin column, Phase 4 device credential security (SHA-256 hashing, rotation), Phase 5 stable IoT identity (device_sensor_mappings, reading_projections), Phase 6 unified ingestion provenance, Phase 7 alert/data integrity (AlertRuleValidationService), Phase 8 production maturity (audit_logs table). Frontend: auth store RBAC getters, route requiresPermission, permission-based UI visibility.
nodes.rationale: Documents the complete RBAC and security remediation implementation. Defines the permission system (device.view, sensor.create, alert.resolve, etc.), the authorization architecture (users → roles → permissions → policies), and the device credential hashing strategy.

nodes.label: Backend Agent Definition (iot-back-implementador)
nodes.description: Claude agent definition for Laravel 12 backend implementation. Defines conventions: controllers call application services, services own model/domain transitions, observers own side effects. G0D ownership consolidation rule. AlertService is alert-rule evaluation owner. DeviceService handles device transitions. EventServiceProvider centralizes wiring. Redis Streams are the durable event backbone. Three rate limit tiers: api-read (120/min), api-write (60/min), auth-login (5/min).
nodes.rationale: Establishes the backend agent's conventions and ownership rules for the IoT platform. Defines the architectural layering (controllers → services → models → observers → events) and the G0D consolidation gate that precedes all implementation.

nodes.label: Frontend Agent Definition (iot-front-implementador)
nodes.description: Claude agent definition for Vue 3 SPA implementation. Single Echo instance per tab via echo.js. Channel registry for subscription lifecycle. Alert projection owner is alerts.js store. SensorMonitorBoard owns merge/history/MAX_POINTS. Reuse base components and formatters.js. Mobile-first target: 320/360/390/430 phone, 768 tablet, 1440 desktop. No polling fallback. Lifecycle-triggered recovery.
nodes.rationale: Defines the frontend agent conventions: single Echo connection, alert projection ownership, and mobile-first responsive targets. Critical for understanding the realtime architecture and component ownership boundaries.

nodes.label: Docker Compose Stack Definition
nodes.description: 8-service Docker Compose stack. Base profile: db (MySQL 8, ROW binlog, 7-day retention), redis (7-alpine, AOF everysec), back (Laravel), front (Vite SPA). Workers profile: debezium (CDC from binlog), outbox-cdc-consumer (XREADGROUP/XAUTOCLAIM from CDC streams), raw-consumer (raw:consume --block=5000), domain-event-consumer (domain:consume --block=5000). Optional queue profile: queue (php artisan queue:work). Ingestion service: Python MQTT adapter. Volumes: db_data, redis_data, back_vendor, front_node_modules, ingestion_spool. Healthchecks on all core services. DEBEZIUM_DB_PASSWORD required.
nodes.rationale: Defines the complete Docker infrastructure. Shows the CDC pipeline topology (MySQL binlog → Debezium → CDC streams → consumers), the worker profiles, and the healthcheck dependencies. Critical for understanding the deployment architecture.

nodes.label: Final Audit Report (2026-09-10)
nodes.description: Audit from 2026-09-10 with 16 findings: 2 CRITICAL (C1: .env.testing with real APP_KEY, C2: leaked env backup CLOSED), 4 HIGH (H1: SMTP plaintext in system_settings, H2: default DB credentials, H3: no CI/CD, H4: stale docs), 4 MEDIUM (M1: console.log in Vue, M2: ingestion_service no retry, M3: large components, M4: binary files committed), 6 LOW/INFO. Execution GAP: backend tests not executed (no PHP/MySQL/Redis on Windows). What went well: event-driven architecture, polling eliminated, realtime delivery, database design, 580 tests at 99% pass rate, Docker Compose, accessibility, ADR documentation.
nodes.rationale: The most recent comprehensive audit. Identifies security vulnerabilities (APP_KEY exposure, SMTP credentials), CI gaps, and documents the test suite status. The 580 tests at 99% pass rate is the key quality metric.

nodes.label: Raw-First Ingestion Pipeline Documentation
nodes.description: Documents the implemented durable ingestion path. Entry contracts: POST /api/ingestion/events (middleware ingestion.token, persists raw receipt + outbox, returns 201 received), POST /api/sensors/{sensor}/readings (API key, creates reading directly), MQTT (ingestion_service validates and forwards). Durable path: IngestionController → MySQL (raw_sensor_events + raw_event_outboxes) → Debezium binlog capture → iot-cdc.* streams → cdc:consume-outboxes → iot.raw-events → raw:consume (normalizes readings, updates raw_sensor_events status) → domain_event_outboxes → Debezium → iot.domain-events → domain:consume → Pusher-compatible broadcast. Consumer groups: raw-process-v1, browser-delivery-v1, email-delivery-v1. Processes: cdc:consume-outboxes --block=5000, raw:consume --block=5000, domain:consume --block=5000.
nodes.rationale: The authoritative document for the ingestion pipeline. Defines the exact flow from ingestion to browser delivery, the consumer groups, the persistence states, and the process commands. Supersedes any earlier pipeline descriptions.

nodes.label: Pending Optimizations Backlog
nodes.description: 7 prioritized optimization items, each with 4 acceptance gates (baseline evidence, focused tests, staged rollout, post-change comparison). Items: 1) Benchmark/simplify AlertService queries, 2) Retire Blade by vertical with API-parity tests, 3) Split SensorApiController by responsibility, 4) Decompose SensorMonitorBoard.vue, 5) Evaluate persistent MQTT client in script_datos.py, 6) Retain central models and shared reading ownership, 7) Add measured ingest/query observability. Non-negotiable preservation: route contracts, reconnect/queue/ordering behavior, Sensor/Device/User ownership, error signals.
nodes.rationale: Defines the optimization backlog with strict evidence-based acceptance criteria. Prevents premature optimization by requiring baseline measurement before any change. Critical for understanding what NOT to change without evidence.

nodes.label: OpenAPI 3.0.3 Specification
nodes.description: OpenAPI spec for IoT Platform API. Rate limits: api-read 120/min, api-write 60/min, auth-login 5/min. Security schemes: bearerAuth (Sanctum), deviceKey (X-Device-Key header). Endpoints: Health (/api/health), Auth (login, register, forgot-password, reset-password, verify-email, me, logout, resend-verification), IoT (GET /api/iot/sensors, POST /api/sensors/{sensor}/readings, POST /api/ingestion/events), Sensors (CRUD + readings + export + latest-readings + series + graph-zones), Devices (CRUD + status + sensors + sensor-list), Alerts (list, active, unresolved, resolve-all, detail, resolve), AlertRules (CRUD), Dashboard (metrics, preferences), Profile, Admin (metrics, users, roles, labs, sensor-types, device-types, config alerts/general/email, system-info, internal metrics).
nodes.rationale: The API contract definition. Maps every endpoint to its access level and request/response schemas. Critical for understanding the complete API surface and its authorization boundaries.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Records (ADR G1)
nodes.description: 4 ADRs backed by Redis 7 spike (INTEGRATION_VERIFIED). ADR-1: Durable publication = transactional outbox + binlog CDC with durable offsets. Rejected DB::afterCommit()-only (process can die after commit). afterCommit() kept as latency hint only. Schema-level idempotency: unique (source, source_event_id) on raw_sensor_events, unique (sensor_reading_id, alert_rule_id) on alerts. ADR-2: Client recovery = lean V1 lifecycle-triggered one-shot authenticated snapshot + resubscribe. No periodic GET. ADR-3: DLQ = dedicated iot.dead-letter-events stream (spike-proven). failed_jobs acceptable for queue relay failures. Batch 100, 5 attempts, bounded backoff. ADR-4: Internal fan-out = direct browser-delivery-v1 consumer → Pusher-compatible broadcaster. No Redis Pub/Sub until horizontal scaling needed.
nodes.rationale: The architecture decisions that bind all implementation stages. ADR-1 is the most critical: it defines the entire publication topology and rejects the simpler afterCommit()-only approach with a concrete justification.

nodes.label: Chart Color Zones Fix (2026-09-11)
nodes.description: Fix for chart semantic zone colors. Backend projects zones from RuleToGraphZones; frontend paints with SINOA tokens. Demo server lacked bands for sensors; buildZonesViewModel converted absence to neutral gray. Added explicit synthetic intervals to demo server (not modifying backend rules/data). Chart now reserves margin outside configured limits to show outer bands. CacheDir separated by mode to avoid Vite 504 collisions. Verification: 34 tests correct (zoneBackgroundPlugin, graphZonesProjection, chartTheme, SensorReadingChart); Chrome headless checks 100+ pixels per canvas at 1440 and 390px.
nodes.rationale: Documents the chart zone color implementation and verification. Shows the integration between RuleToGraphZones (backend), buildZonesViewModel (frontend), and SINOA token system.

nodes.label: Gate 10 Evidence (CDC Pipeline Verified)
nodes.description: Gate 10 substantially closed. Live Docker CDC pipeline verified end to end: POST /api/ingestion/events → raw_sensor_events + raw_event_outboxes(pending) → Debezium binlog → iot-cdc.* → outbox-cdc-consumer → iot.raw-events → raw-consumer normalized → 2 sensor_readings created → domain_event_outboxes → domain:consume delivered (2/2, 0 pending). Two real bugs found and fixed: Debezium config mount path (v3.5 reads /debezium/config/), Redis stream key-prefix mismatch (publishers used Laravel facade prefix, consumers used raw commands). Backend: 303 tests, 0 failed, 1170 assertions (isolated SQLite + Redis 6399). Frontend: 182 tests, 0 failures; build green; no-polling gate PASS; Playwright 53/53 clean. Observability: EventPipelineMetricsService::snapshot() with stream/consumer/outbox counters. Outstanding: scripted CDC fault injection A-E, formal network-quiet capture, remote CI execution.
nodes.rationale: The most critical evidence document. Proves the CDC pipeline works end to end on the live Docker stack, documents the two real bugs found and fixed, and provides the test evidence for Gate 10 closure.

Gate 7: AlertService creates alert + alert.triggered in one DB::transaction, AlertObserver removed sync broadcast, DomainEventBroadcastConsumer handles alert.triggered with idempotent redelivery, frontend bounded seenTriggeredIds/seenResolvedIds ledgers, recovery buffers resolved events. nodes.label: Graph Semantic Zones Plan
nodes.description: AlertRule is the threshold source of truth for chart zones. Semantic mapping: green (no rule violated), amber (warning rule), red (danger rule), info (info rule, separate band), neutral (no applicable rule). Precedence: danger > warning > info > normal. Frozen boundary semantics (GRAPH-004): AlertService inclusive semantics (value <= min_value or value >= max_value). Architecture: AlertRule → AlertService rule-resolution → RuleToGraphZones normalizer (NEW, single owner) → public/authenticated projection → SensorReadingChart. Vue must not reimplement AlertService. Public exposure: only graph-safe projection (ordered severity intervals {from, to, severity}), no rule ids, no scope. Issue backlog: GRAPH-001 through GRAPH-013, TEST-001 through TEST-005. Done when: one server-owned normalizer, chart paints green/amber/red/neutral, no-rules renders neutral, tests pass.
nodes.rationale: Defines the chart semantic zones architecture. Establishes AlertRule as the single source of truth, the precedence rules, and the normalizer pattern that prevents Vue from reimplementing AlertService evaluation.

nodes.label: Authorization Consistency Fix (Phase C)
nodes.rationale: ResourceAccessService::canViewSensorReadings() established as single telemetry authority using sensor_reading.view; routes/channels.php sensor.{id} routes through it; four-cell matrix (view x reading.view) plus WS authorize/deny parity tests.

nodes.rationale: REST reading actions still reach SensorPolicy::view (requiring sensor.view) while the private WebSocket channel requires sensor_reading.view, creating a REST/WS permission divergence.

nodes.rationale: composer audit 44 advisories reduced to 0 via laravel/framework v12.10.2 to v12.69.2 upgrade; npm audit 5 reduced to 3 moderate dev-only via immutable high patch.

nodes.label: allReadings Global Bounds Fix (Phase E)
nodes.rationale: ALL_READINGS_GLOBAL_ROW_BUDGET = 5000 hard global ceiling; per-sensor limit = floor(budget / sensorCount) (min 1). Validate from/to/limit with controlled 422.

nodes.label: allReadings Global Bounds Bug
nodes.rationale: max(1, floor(5000 / sensorCount)) gives every loaded sensor at least one row, so more than 5,000 sensors can exceed the claimed 5,000-row ceiling. The sensor object list itself is unbounded.

nodes.rationale: Enforces the no-polling architecture on every push/PR via a static AST scan that fails if any tracked source file contains product-state polling constructs (setInterval, setTimeout with REST/WS calls, pusher fallback loops).

nodes.label: Poison-to-DLQ Live Certification (Phase H4)
nodes.rationale: Unmapped event retried 5x then dead-lettered to iot.dead-letter-events with full diagnostic; poison event did not stall the partition — events 2/3/4 processed normally around it.

nodes.label: Transactional Outbox Pattern
nodes.rationale: Chosen via ADR-1 for durable publication: persist events in the database transaction (outbox), then relay via binlog CDC to Redis Streams.

nodes.label: CDC Pipeline — Debezium + Redis Streams + Outbox
nodes.norm_label: cdc pipeline — debezium + redis streams + outbox
nodes.rationale: ADR-1 selects transactional outbox + binlog-driven CDC with durable offsets as the final durable-publication topology. The transitional Laravel relay/scanner is retired; delivery is Debezium CDC to Redis stream to cdc:consume-outboxes.

nodes.label: ADR-1 — Durable Publication
nodes.rationale: Selects transactional outbox + binlog CDC + Redis Streams with durable offsets as the final durable-publication topology.

nodes.label: MySQL Mapping Concurrency Proof (Phase D)
nodes.rationale: lockForUpdate() over dsm_temporal_lookup_idx acquires InnoDB next-key/gap locks that serialize even the empty-set insert. 100 iterations, 0 violations, COUNT(open)=1 every time.

nodes.label: Transactional Integrity Fix (Phase B)
nodes.rationale: Four atomicity items fixed: B1 device provisioning, B2 sensor provisioning, B3 device update, B4 device delete each wrapped in transactions with forced-failure regression tests.
